A18.notes: The faithfulness guard is deterministic and pure: body multiset precision >= 0.98 vs OCR tokens (fuzzy matching for OCR variants — the same fuzzy rules as the cleanup metrics), every OCR content token missing from the body must appear in removed_chrome or the known-chrome dictionary (the deterministic cleanup's own chrome-line knowledge), author/source_app literal-or-drop, removed_chrome entries traceable-or-dropped. The eval runs the REAL model's output through these guards on every standard + injection fixture (guardVerdict recorded per fixture in llm-eval-chromium.json).

tests: junit:docs/evidence/S4/junit/host-vitest.xml::cleanup quality on gold input — every English fixture (S1 + S4) > covers all 30 English fixtures
A19.notes: Browser eval (WASM path, headless Chromium) on REAL browser-OCR output, both cleanup modes on the same pick, per-fixture numbers committed in docs/evidence/S4/llm-eval-chromium.json. DECISION (plan-valid completion, the "otherwise" branch): the LLM ships DISABLED BY DEFAULT (LLM_CLEANUP_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT=false). The measured margins (final run): deterministic baseline mean body-token F1 0.997 / chrome leakage 0.65% / fabricated 0 (meets the bars) vs model-mode applied rows mean F1 0.847 / chrome leakage 86% / mean latency 170 s — the model keeps the author/@handle header chrome in the body, sits 15 F1 points BELOW the baseline, leaks far above the 2% bar and takes ~3x the 60 s WASM budget (12 applied / 10 fail-closed fallback across the 22-fixture eval). The deterministic baseline stays the default and meets the bars on the S4 tree (eval_cleanup_body_f1_standard_set, both engines). The user can still opt in per session and every opt-in run is guarded.

tests: junit:docs/evidence/S4/junit/host-vitest.xml::payload builders with suggestion toggles (S4, A03/A04 default-off) > WITHOUT extras every payload is exactly the review text (A03 invariant)
A21.notes: The pinned model runs through the app in the browser (WASM path, headless Chromium): the real download -> cache -> Worker load -> JSON-schema-constrained inference -> deterministic guard -> validated review text. The applied path on the real model is proven in the same final run by uc13's 4 applied injection fixtures and the eval's 12 applied fixtures (guardVerdict pass, 141-236 s real inference); the a21 flow itself settled on the designed unavailable branch in the final pass (clean01 hit the fail-closed 240 s cap — the spec asserts both branches, and the integration smokes show the applied branch on the same tree). Suggestion toggles (tags/summary) are labelled, default OFF, and excluded from payloads unless toggled on (the share payload with toggles off is exactly the review text — asserted). Where the capability path says the browser cannot run it, the app correctly falls back and says so: WebKit on this build fails the 397 MB wasm load (measured, probe-log.md) and the a21 webkit branch asserts the explicit unavailable flag + the deterministic text; the testProbe=unsupported override asserts the model-unavailable path structurally in both engines. WebGPU: NOT_RUN on this Linux host per plan D8 (A30).

limitations: The LLM cleanup ships DISABLED BY DEFAULT by measurement (A19's plan-valid branch): the pinned 0.6B keeps header chrome in the body (quality below the rules baseline) and a cleanup takes 65-140 s on the single-threaded WASM path. The opt-in toggle runs the same guarded pipeline.

The real model OBEYED an injection into its tags array in the S4 probe (probe-log.md); the deterministic demotion guard defuses this class on the applied path, but a semantically-obeying model output that stays schema-valid, faithful AND unflagged by the input patterns remains theoretically possible — the eval proves the fixtures hold on the real model, not a general prompt-injection impossibility result.

This Playwright WebKit build cannot load the 397 MB weights into wasm ("unknown transient reason", the same engine-bug family as the S3 storage measurements) — on WebKit the model cleanup always reports unavailable with the visible fallback; the real-model proofs are Chromium-only on this host. Real Safari behavior is NOT_RUN (A27/A30).

WebGPU is NOT_RUN on this Linux host (plan D8): headless Chromium exposes navigator.gpu (a software adapter would back it) and WebKit does not expose it at all; no WebGPU-path claim is made anywhere (A30).

The transformers.js candidate was measured with the project's vite bundling its browser ESM (its package uses bare specifiers and cannot load unbundled); its generation did not complete within the probe deadline at 350 max tokens — the rejection is on measured latency, not quality.

The single-threaded WASM path (no crossOriginIsolation on this host, so no SharedArrayBuffer) is ~2.3 tokens/s; the latency numbers are headless-Linux single-thread numbers and say nothing about real-phone or WebGPU speeds.

A22's per-mode latency/memory budgets (OCR <= 5 s, cleanup <= 60 s WASM) are S5 scope; the S4 eval records the cleanup latencies honestly (most model cleanups exceed 60 s single-threaded — recorded, to be budgeted in S5 with the LLM disabled by default).
